cases.sentence: Красивый ___ с черной с проседью бородой неподвижно стоял, держа чашку с медом.
cases.translation: The handsome old man with a graying black beard stood motionless, holding a cup of honey.
cases.explain: Старик is the subject of стоял (stood), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Никто не объявлял ___, а люди просто сочувствуют страданиям ближних.
cases.translation: No one declared war, but people simply sympathize with the suffering of their neighbors.
cases.explain: A negated transitive verb (не объявлял) takes its object in the genitive case: войны.

cases.sentence: Люди сочувствуют чужому ___ и желают помочь ближнему.
cases.translation: People sympathize with a stranger's suffering and wish to help their neighbor.
cases.explain: The verb сочувствовать (to sympathize with) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович осторожно вынимал из чашки живую ___, попавшую в мед.
cases.translation: Sergei Ivanovich carefully took out of the cup a live bee that had fallen into the honey.
cases.explain: The verb вынимал (was taking out) governs the accusative case for its direct object.

cases.sentence: Старик неподвижно стоял, держа чашку с ___.
cases.translation: The old man stood motionless, holding a cup of honey.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: В восьмидесятимиллионном ___ всегда найдутся десятки тысяч людей, потерявших общественное положение.
cases.translation: Among eighty million people there will always be found tens of thousands who have lost their social standing.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in/among) governs the prepositional case here.

reading.ru: «А ты знаешь, Костя, с кем Сергей Иванович ехал сюда?» — сказал Долли, отделив детей огурцами и медом.
reading.question: What news does Dolly share with Levin (Kostya) about who Sergei Ivanovich was traveling with?
options: That he was traveling with Vronsky
That he was traveling with Kitty
That he was traveling with the old prince
reading.correct: That he was traveling with Vronsky
reading.explain: Dolly asks Kostya if he knows who Sergei Ivanovich traveled with, having given the children cucumbers and honey to distract them.

reading.question: Where is Vronsky going, according to Dolly?
reading.explain: Dolly says Sergei Ivanovich traveled with Vronsky, who is going to Serbia.

reading.question: How did Levin react to hearing that Vronsky was leading a squadron at his own expense?
reading.explain: Levin remarked, "That suits him," about Vronsky leading a squadron at his own expense.

reading.ru: — С турками, — спокойно улыбаясь, отвечал Сергей Иванович, выпроставший беспомощно двигавшую ножками почерневшую от меда пчелу и ссаживая ее с ножа на крепкий осиновый листок.
reading.question: What was Sergei Ivanovich doing with the bee stuck in the honey?
options: Carefully freeing it with a knife and setting it on a leaf
reading.correct: Carefully freeing it with a knife and setting it on a leaf
reading.explain: While calmly answering that they were fighting the Turks, he freed the honey-covered bee with his knife and set it on an aspen leaf.

reading.ru: Никто не объявлял войны, а люди сочувствуют страданиям ближних и желают помочь им, сказал Сергей Иванович.
reading.question: According to Sergei Ivanovich, why are people going to help, even though no war was declared?
options: Because people sympathize with the suffering of their neighbors and want to help them
Because the government ordered them to
reading.correct: Because people sympathize with the suffering of their neighbors and want to help them
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich explains that no war was declared, but people sympathize with the suffering of others and wish to help.

reading.ru: «Да это и не пчела, это оса», — сказал Левин.
reading.question: What insect did Dolly mistake for a bee?
reading.explain: Levin corrects Dolly, saying it isn't a bee but a wasp.

reading.ru: Война, с одной стороны, есть такое животное, жестокое, ужасное дело, что ни один человек, не говорю уже христианин, не может лично взять на свою ответственность начало войны.
reading.question: How does Levin describe war?
options: As such a brutal, terrible affair that no person, let alone a Christian, could take responsibility for starting one
As a noble and glorious undertaking
As something only governments should discuss
As a necessary evil that everyone should support
reading.correct: As such a brutal, terrible affair that no person, let alone a Christian, could take responsibility for starting one
reading.explain: Levin argues that war is such a brutal and terrible affair that no individual, let alone a Christian, could take personal responsibility for starting one.

reading.ru: «В том-то и штука, батюшка, что могут быть случаи, когда правительство не исполняет воли граждан, и тогда общество заявляет свою волю», — сказал Котовасов.
reading.question: What point does Katavasov make about government and the will of the people?
options: That there can be cases when the government fails to carry out the people's will, and then society expresses its own will
That the government always represents the people perfectly
That society should never oppose the government
That war is only just when declared officially
reading.correct: That there can be cases when the government fails to carry out the people's will, and then society expresses its own will
reading.explain: Katavasov argues that sometimes government fails to carry out the citizens' will, and then society expresses its will directly.

reading.question: What atrocity does Sergei Ivanovich say is being committed against fellow Slavs and fellow believers?
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich says brothers of the same blood and faith are being killed.

reading.question: When Sergei Ivanovich pressed Levin about defending a woman being beaten, what did Levin say he would NOT do?
reading.explain: Levin says he would intervene but would not kill the attacker.

reading.ru: Я жил за границей, читал газеты и, признаюсь, еще до болгарских ужасов никак не понимал, почему все русские так вдруг полюбили братьев-славян, а я никакой к ним любви не чувствую.
reading.question: What did the old prince say about his own feelings toward the Slavic brothers before the Bulgarian atrocities?
options: That he lived abroad, read the papers, and never understood why Russians suddenly loved their Slavic brothers, since he felt no such love himself
That he always felt deep love for the Slavs
That he never read any news about it
That he supported the war from the very beginning
reading.correct: That he lived abroad, read the papers, and never understood why Russians suddenly loved their Slavic brothers, since he felt no such love himself
reading.explain: The old prince admits he lived abroad, read the papers, and could not understand the sudden love for the Slavic brothers, feeling none himself.

reading.ru: «Личные мнения тут ничего не значат», — сказал Сергей Иванович.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich say about the value of personal opinions in this matter?
options: That personal opinions mean nothing here
That personal opinions are the most important thing
That only the Tsar's opinion matters
reading.correct: That personal opinions mean nothing here
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich states that personal opinions mean nothing in this matter.

reading.ru: «Да извините меня, я этого не вижу. Народ и знать не знает», — сказал князь.
reading.question: How did the old prince respond to the claim that the people had expressed their will?
options: He said he didn't see it that way, and that the people don't even know about it
He said the people had voted on it
reading.correct: He said he didn't see it that way, and that the people don't even know about it
reading.explain: The prince responds that he doesn't see it that way, and that the common people don't even know about it.

reading.ru: Красивый старик с черной с проседью бородой и густыми серебряными волосами неподвижно стоял, держа чашку с медом, ласково и спокойно с высоты своего роста, глядя на господ, очевидно, ничего не понимая и не желая понимать.
reading.question: How is the old beekeeper described as he stood listening to the conversation?
options: A handsome old man with a graying black beard and silvery hair, standing calmly, clearly not understanding or caring to understand
reading.correct: A handsome old man with a graying black beard and silvery hair, standing calmly, clearly not understanding or caring to understand
reading.explain: The old beekeeper is described as handsome, with a graying black beard and silvery hair, standing calmly and clearly not understanding the debate.

reading.ru: «Значит, по-моему, — сказал начинавший горячиться Левин, — что в восьмидесятимиллионном народе всегда найдутся не сотни, как теперь, а десятки тысяч людей, потерявших общественное положение.
reading.question: What does Levin argue about the number of people who actually understand or care about the Slavic cause, out of eighty million?
options: That only tens of thousands, not the whole nation, truly know or care about it
That every single Russian understands it perfectly
That no one cares at all
That only the aristocracy understands it
reading.correct: That only tens of thousands, not the whole nation, truly know or care about it
reading.explain: Growing heated, Levin argues that among eighty million people there will always be tens of thousands who have lost their social standing, not the whole nation acting as one.
